description: Mexico's former telecom regulator, the Instituto Federal de Telecomunicaciones, published interactive maps of 4G (LTE) mobile coverage built from crowdsourced measurements. The data come from Ookla Cell Analytics, collected from users' phones, tablets and computers connected to cellular networks between 1 November 2024 and 31 January 2025, and consist only of network performance measurements that do not identify any person. The maps are hosted on the Felt web mapping platform with user manuals for desktop and mobile devices. The IFT website is now a historical archive, since the regulator's functions passed to the Comisión Reguladora de Telecomunicaciones. Coverage: Mexico. Format and access: interactive web map, free to view; no download of the underlying data was found. Caveats: coverage appears only where users measured, so areas with service but no users look uncovered; operators and spatial units were not stated on the page read; the IFT telecom information bank (BIT) no longer resolves. Simulation uses: evidence of real 4G service to validate coverage models and to spot areas without measured service for emergency planning. Related records: the Ookla open data and the LAC-IX exchange survey cover the region, and the Colombian CRC mobile infrastructure coverage data are a comparable regulator dataset.
